scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator, a man with glasses and a beard, speaks directly to the camera, explaining Instagram's new features. Overlaid text and graphical representations of Instagram features (repost, visible likes, location map) appear on screen.
scene_timeline.audio_description: The creator states that Instagram added a repost button, visible likes on Reels, and a location map because they are desperate to make the platform appear to have real people on it.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
The reason Instagram added a repost button
I love this vibe
and visible likes on reels
and a location map
to make it look like their platform still has real people on it

scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator continues to speak to the camera, gesturing with his hands. A citation for a Forbes article appears on screen, supporting his claims about AI-generated content.
scene_timeline.audio_description: The creator explains that users initially joined Instagram to connect with friends, but randomized feeds and 'slop' were introduced. He cites Forbes, stating that 70% of social media posts are now AI-generated.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
I mean,
we all came to Instagram
to connect with our friends,
but then they randomized our feeds
and crammed slop down our throats,
and now, according to Forbes,
70% of all social media posts are AI generated
Drenik, Gary. “The Secret to Profitability in Gen AI Lies in Customer Centricity.” Forbes. April 1, 2025.

scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator maintains eye contact with the camera, expressing concern and disappointment through his facial expressions and gestures.
scene_timeline.audio_description: He elaborates that this situation is causing increasing disillusionment among users who seek human connection on the platform but are consistently disappointed.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
That's making us
increasingly disillusioned with the platform
to go on there
to find human connection
and yet are consistently disappointed

scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator continues to speak, with two more academic citations appearing on screen, reinforcing his argument about Instagram's legitimacy crisis.
scene_timeline.audio_description: The creator states that fewer people are posting online, leading to Instagram facing a 'legitimacy crisis' where they need to convince users they are still a form of 'social media' for friends.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
As a result,
fewer people are posting online,
and Instagram is facing a legitimacy crisis
where they need ways to convince you
that they are still a form of "social media"
between you and your friends
Kay, Katty. “Why Did Our Friends Stop Posting on Social Media?” BBC. July 23, 2025.
Cite
Abiri, Gilad, and Sebastián Guidi. “From a Network to a Dilemma: The Legitimacy of Social Media.” Stem. Tech. L. Rev. 58 (2026): 62.

scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator uses hand gestures to emphasize his points while discussing the manipulative nature of Instagram's features.
scene_timeline.audio_description: He calls the Snap Map rip-off obvious, but describes the repost and visible like features as 'insidious' because they create the impression that algorithmically recommended content is validated by real people you know.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
And the rip-off of the Snap Map is obvious,
But the repost and visible like features
are far more insidious
because they're meant to give the impression
that your algorithmically recommended content
has somehow been validated
by real people you know

scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator continues his explanation, with another academic citation appearing on screen.
scene_timeline.audio_description: He explains that this makes it feel more acceptable to consume 'slop' if friends appear to have endorsed it, creating an illusion of social interaction that isn't real.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
It feels more okay to consume slop
if you see that your friends have signed off on it,
because that creates the illusion
that you're still having a social interaction,
even though you're really not
Castelló, Itziar, Michael Etter, and Finn Arup Nielsen. “Strategizing Legitimacy: How social media platforms gain legitimacy.” Journal of management studies 53.3 (2016): 402-432.

scene_timeline.visual_description: The creator concludes his argument, maintaining a direct address to the viewer.
scene_timeline.audio_description: He introduces the technique of 'discursive legitimation,' where social media platforms appear more legitimate by presenting themselves as neutral connectors rather than intermediaries. He warns that every reposted video means one less real post from someone you care about.
scene_timeline.text_on_screen:
This is a technique called "discursive legitimation,"
and social media platforms
appear more legitimate
like neutral institutions
connecting networks of people together,
rather than intermediaries
affecting everything we see
But just remember that
every time you see a reposted video
is one time you're not seeing a real post
by someone you care about

parsed_output.overall_summary: This video critically analyzes Instagram's recent feature additions, such as the repost button, visible likes on Reels, and a location map, arguing they are a desperate attempt to mask a decline in genuine user engagement. The creator explains that Instagram's shift from connecting friends to prioritizing algorithmic content and AI-generated posts has led to user disillusionment and a 'legitimacy crisis'. He introduces the concept of 'discursive legitimation,' where platforms create an illusion of social interaction and neutrality to maintain their perceived value, ultimately warning that these features displace authentic content from real connections.

takeaways.statement: Instagram's new features like the repost button, visible likes, and location map are a desperate attempt to create the illusion of real user activity and social connection on a platform facing declining genuine engagement.
Social media platforms, including Instagram, are experiencing a 'legitimacy crisis' due to the prevalence of algorithmic feeds and AI-generated content, leading to user disillusionment.

The technique of 'discursive legitimation' is employed by social media platforms to appear as neutral institutions connecting people, rather than intermediaries controlling content, thereby maintaining their perceived legitimacy.
Every reposted video on Instagram signifies a missed opportunity to see genuine content from people a user cares about, further eroding authentic social interaction.
